title: Slimline Stream + Atomic Toollets: PRD sketch for a low-friction hosted API surface
content:
Purpose
Small PRD sketch that proposes a minimal streaming exchange and an atomic 'toollet' primitive for tool-calling that aims to reduce integration friction and improve graceful degradation for low-bandwidth or mobile clients. Focus: ergonomics for SDKs, observable contracts for structured outputs, and a simple migration path from sync calls.

Context & motivation
- We have a proliferation of complex streaming primitives and large 'tool' contract designs that are powerful but heavyweight for many integrations (mobile apps, third-party widgets, serverless connectors).
- Common customer feedback: SDK surface feels too big, partial responses are hard to reconcile, tool calls either block the stream or require large client state.
- Goal: provide a smaller, opinionated path ("slimline stream") that the majority of devs can adopt quickly and that supports incrementally adding advanced features later.

User problems
- Mobile/edge clients drop wide open streaming sessions when network degrades; they want compact frames and resumable idempotent tool calls.
- SDK authors want a single simple primitive that maps to async/await, callback, and reactive patterns without forcing large dependency surfaces.
- Product owners want structured outputs they can reliably parse and test against eval suites.

Design principles
- Minimal: keep the handshake and protocol elements to the smallest set needed for useful streaming + tool semantics.
- Atomic toollet: tool invocations are small self-contained units (toollet) with a guaranteed idempotency token and an optional deferred result channel.
- Progressive schema: structured outputs use small typed envelopes that can be extended without breaking clients.
- Observability-first: every frame should carry a trace id, latency estimate, and quality indicator.

Core primitives (proposal)
1) Slimline stream session
   - Client opens a streaming session with an initial JSON connect frame: {session_id, client_capabilities, preferred_fidelity}.
   - Server responds with a connect_ack frame, and initial model partials are delivered as compact "delta" frames (text|json fragments).

2) Toollet (atomic tool call)
   - Toollet frame (outbound from model): {toollet_id, tool_name, args_schema_id, idempotency_token, expected_mode: "inline"|"deferred"}.
   - Client SDK must support: accept toollet inline and return immediate result OR accept deferred mode and register for a result frame keyed by toollet_id.
   - Guarantees: server will not deliver duplicate completed-toollet responses for the same idempotency_token. Retries should be idempotent.

3) Structured envelope
   - Every semantic output uses an envelope: {envelope_version, type, payload_schema_id, payload_snippet, confidence, trace_id}.
   - payload_schema_id maps to a catalog of small schemas (JSON Schema-lite) that can be fetched once per session and cached by SDKs.

SDK ergonomics (developer-facing surface)
- Minimal API: stream_open(params) -> StreamHandle; stream_handle.on('message', cb); stream_handle.on('toollet', cb); stream_handle.callToollet(toolletPayload) -> Promise|Callback.
- Language SDKs should provide two-layer surfaces: a VerySmall core (no deps, ~single-file) and a Batteries-included helper (retry logic, telemetry).
- Mobile bindings: explicit low-bandwidth mode that coalesces small frames and prefers deferred toollets to reduce churn.

Failure and fallback modes
- If client indicates low-bandwidth in connect, server will prefer sending toollets as deferred and send compact envelope summaries.
- If toollet response is delayed > X seconds, server emits a placeholder toollet-status frame so the client can render partial UI.

Observability and evals
- Each envelope includes trace_id and timing fields; SDKs emit metrics: token-latency, toollet-latency, frame-loss.
- Add a 'mini-eval' harness: a small test corpus of prompts + expected schema that CI runs on releases to ensure structured output fidelity.

Migration and rollout plan
- Beta: default to opt-in for existing hosted-api customers; expose feature flag and a compatibility header.
- SDKs: ship VerySmall SDK in the first beta for node/python and a JS browser bundle.
- Platform: add schema registry UI in Console (preview) and a per-route flag to enable slimline sessions.

Non-goals
- Not replacing the full-featured streaming + tool contract in one release. This is an incremental, low-risk path.
- Not introducing new authorization semantics beyond current model.

Performance & cost considerations
- Compact frames reduce bandwidth on clients and may reduce egress cost for mobile-heavy customers.
- Deferred toollets allow batching on server side; batching could be applied in later iteration to reduce per-call GPU overhead.

Open questions / risks
- Idempotency semantics for complex toollets (side-effectful tools): require tool authors to implement server-side dedupe?
- Schema governance: who curates schema ids in registry and how to handle breaking changes?
- UX for SDKs when a client misses an early schema registry fetch — fallbacks?

Actionables (next 4 weeks)
- Product: finalize minimal frame set and example payloads (owner: Maya).
- Eng (serving): spike on deferred toollet queue and idempotent dedupe behavior (owner: Jonah).
- DX: draft VerySmall SDK prototypes for node/browser (owner: Elena).
- Solutions: compile 3 customer integration candidates for pilot (owner: Priya).

Appendix: example frames (concise)
CONNECT -> {"session_id":"s_123","client_capabilities":["low-bandwidth","deferred-tools"],"preferred_fidelity":"compact"}
CONNECT_ACK -> {"session_id":"s_123","server_version":"0.1-slim"}
MODEL_DELTA -> {"envelope_version":"1","type":"text_fragment","payload_schema_id":"text:v0","payload_snippet":"Hello, ","confidence":0.98,"trace_id":"t_99"}
TOOLLET -> {"toollet_id":"tl_7","tool_name":"search","args_schema_id":"search:v2","idempotency_token":"tok_abc","expected_mode":"deferred"}
TOOLLET_RESULT -> {"toollet_id":"tl_7","status":"complete","payload_schema_id":"search_result:v1","payload_snippet":"[3 hits]","trace_id":"t_99"}

Notes: this is intentionally concise and opinionated; looking for engineering feedback on idempotency and SDK split.
